newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SET TO DETHRONE NIEMANN WITH SLAP-SKATE.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SET TO DETHRONE NIEMANN WITH SLAP-SKATE.

text.p: Dutch female speed skaters triumphed on Saturday's first day of the second World Cup event this winter season, putting another dent in the throne of reigning world champion Germany's Gunda Niemann.
Niemann, nurturing world records at 3,000 and 5,000 metres, lost by over a full second to Dutch Tonny de Jong at the 3,000 metres race.
De Jong won in 4 minutes 17.01 seconds while another young Dutch talent, Barbara de Loor, ended second at 4:17.90, breaking her personal best by three seconds.
Niemann blamed her poor technique which has worsened since last year. "Conditionally I'm fine, but because I lack technical skills I have to work twice as hard," she said.
It was the first time in almost half a decade that anyone has been able to beat Niemann at her favourite distances.
The Dutch women skaters said their surprising performances at the first two World Cup events was the result of good training and the success of the innovative slap-skate.
The slap-skate's blade flips open like a scissor from under the heel so that skaters have a better push on the ice.
The men's 1,500 metres race was won by Dutchman Ids Postma, exposing excellent form by setting a new track record at 1 minute 52.08 seconds.
Dutch world champion Rintje Ritsma was tracking Postma at less than a second, while 1,500 metres world record holder Japanese Hiroyuki Noake lagged by 1.5 seconds.
